title: The Chessboard & Files/Ranks
description: Learn about the 64 squares, ranks, files, diagonals, and how the board is set up.
objectives: Understand the 8x8 grid structure
Identify files (columns a-h) and ranks (rows 1-8)
Remember the golden rule: 'White on right'

steps.title: Welcome to the 64 Squares
steps.text:
The game of chess is played on an 8x8 grid containing 64 alternating light and dark squares.

Always ensure the bottom-right corner square closest to each player is a light square ('white on right').

steps.title: Files and Ranks
steps.text:
Vertical columns are called 'files', labeled from 'a' to 'h' from left to right (from White's perspective).

Horizontal rows are called 'ranks', numbered from 1 to 8. Rank 1 is White's back rank, and Rank 8 is Black's back rank.

steps.title: Board Knowledge Check
steps.text: Which square is located at the intersection of the 4th file from the left and the 4th rank from White's side?

quizOptions.explanation: c is the 3rd file (a=1, b=2, c=3).
Correct! The 4th file is 'd' and the 4th rank is '4', making it d4 (one of the key central squares).

title: The Mighty Rook
description: Master how the Rook moves in straight lines along files and ranks to dominate open lines.
objectives: Move the Rook horizontally and vertically
Understand the Rook's range across open ranks and files
Capture enemy pieces with the Rook

steps.title: How the Rook Moves
steps.text: The Rook moves as far as it wants forward, backward, left, or right along any rank or file, as long as its path is not blocked by another piece.

steps.title: Exercise: Seize the Open File
steps.text: White has a Rook on d5. Move the Rook to the top rank (d8) to dominate the file.
steps.hint: Click on your Rook on d5, then click on the d8 square at the top of the board.
steps.correctFeedback: Excellent! The Rook controls the entire d-file.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Look for square d8 on the top rank.

steps.title: Exercise: Capture the Black Pawn
steps.text: There is an undefended black pawn on h5. Use your Rook on d5 to capture it!
steps.hint: The Rook captures by moving into the square of an enemy piece. Move horizontally to h5.
steps.correctFeedback: Well played! You captured the pawn on h5.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Move your Rook horizontally across rank 5 to capture on h5.

title: The Leaping Knight
description: Learn the unique L-shaped movement of the Knight and its special power to jump over other pieces.
objectives: Master the Knight's 'L' jump: 2 squares in one direction, then 1 square perpendicular
Remember that Knights can jump over friendly and enemy pieces
Notice how Knights always land on an opposite color square

steps.title: The Knight's Jump
steps.text:
The Knight is the only piece in chess that can jump over other pieces!

It moves in an 'L' shape: two squares in any cardinal direction, then one square perpendicular. If it starts on a light square, it always lands on a dark square, and vice versa.

steps.title: Exercise: Center the Knight
steps.text: Move your White Knight from f3 to d4 into the center of the board.
steps.hint: From f3, move 2 squares left and 1 square up to d4.
steps.correctFeedback: Superb! Knights are at their most powerful when placed in the center.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Target square d4 is two squares to the left and one square forward from f3.

steps.title: Knight Rules Quiz
steps.text: Can a Knight jump over enemy pieces that block its direct line of sight?

quizOptions.text: Yes, the Knight can jump over both friendly and enemy pieces.
quizOptions.explanation: Correct! Knights leap freely over all obstacles, only capturing whatever is on their final destination square.

quizOptions.text: No, it must take the pieces it encounters along the way.
quizOptions.explanation: Knights do not capture pieces they leap over.
Knights can leap over any piece type.

title: The Diagonal Bishop
description: Understand color complexes, long diagonals, and how Bishops operate in pairs.
objectives: Move diagonally as far as the path is clear
Recognize light-squared and dark-squared Bishops
Appreciate the power of open diagonals

steps.title: Diagonal Movement
steps.text:
Bishops move along diagonal lines of the same color square they start on. A light-squared Bishop can never visit a dark square!

Because of this, players start with one Bishop of each color to complement each other.

steps.title: Exercise: Seize the Long Diagonal
steps.text: Move your light-squared Bishop on d5 to the corner on h1.
steps.hint: Slide your Bishop diagonally down and to the right into the bottom-right corner h1.
steps.correctFeedback: Great move! Long diagonals allow Bishops to influence the entire board.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Target square h1 is in the bottom-right corner along the light diagonal.

steps.title: Exercise: Capture the Attacker
steps.text: A black Knight on g4 is menacing your position. Use your dark-squared Bishop on e2 to capture it!
steps.hint: Slide your Bishop on e2 up-right along the dark diagonal to g4.
steps.correctFeedback: Well done! You captured the threatening Knight.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Look for the diagonal path from e2 to g4.

title: The All-Powerful Queen
description: Unleash the strongest piece on the board, combining the powers of Rook and Bishop.
objectives: Combine straight and diagonal movements
Learn why the Queen is worth 9 points
Avoid bringing the Queen out too early where it can be attacked

steps.title: The Queen's Dominion
steps.text: The Queen is the most versatile and valuable piece on the board (worth 9 pawns). She can move in any straight line — vertically, horizontally, or diagonally — as far as squares are unobstructed.

steps.title: Exercise: Queen Infiltration
steps.text: Deliver checkmate on f7 with your Queen, protected by your Bishop on c4!
steps.hint: Your Queen on h5 can move diagonally and vertically. Look at the weak f7 square right next to Black's King.
steps.correctFeedback: Checkmate! The Queen attacks the King at point-blank range, and Black cannot capture because the Bishop defends her.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Capture on f7 with the Queen to deliver checkmate.

title: The Royal King & Castling
description: Protect the most critical piece in chess and master kingside and queenside castling.
objectives: Move the King one square in any direction
Learn the special castling move to safeguard the King
Understand conditions when castling is legal

steps.title: The King's Safety
steps.text: The King can move one square in any direction. Unlike all other pieces, the King can never be captured — if the King is attacked and cannot escape, the game ends in Checkmate!

steps.title: The Special Move: Castling
steps.text:
Castling is the only move where you move TWO pieces in a single turn!

The King moves two squares toward a Rook, and that Rook hops over the King to the adjacent square. This moves the King to safety behind pawns and brings the Rook into play.

steps.title: Exercise: Castle Kingside
steps.text: Castle your White King kingside (O-O) to complete development.
steps.hint: Click your King on e1, then click two squares to the right on g1.
steps.correctFeedback: Excellent! Your King is securely tucked away and your Rook is connected.
steps.incorrectFeedback: To castle kingside, move your King from e1 to g1.

title: The Brave Pawn & Promotion
description: Learn pawn moves, diagonal captures, double-step from starting ranks, and promotion.
objectives: Move pawns 1 step forward (or 2 steps on their first move)
Capture one step diagonally forward
Promote a pawn when it reaches the 8th rank

steps.title: How Pawns March
steps.text: Pawns are the soul of chess! They move straight forward one square, but capture diagonally forward. On its very first move, a pawn has the option to move forward TWO squares.

steps.title: Exercise: Pawn Promotion
steps.text: Your pawn on e7 is on the verge of greatness! Push it to e8 to promote to a Queen.
steps.hint: Push the pawn from e7 to e8. When promoted, choose Queen.
steps.correctFeedback: Phenomenal! A humble pawn became a mighty Queen.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Move your pawn forward to e8.

title: Check, Checkmate & Stalemate
description: Distinguish between being checked, delivering checkmate, and accidental stalemate draws.
objectives: Understand the 3 ways to escape check: Capture, Protect (Block), Run
Deliver checkmate to win the game
Avoid stalemate when winning

steps.title: Escaping Check: CPR
steps.text:
When your King is attacked, you MUST resolve the check immediately using CPR:
- C: Capture the checking piece
- P: Protect (block the line of attack with another piece)
- R: Run away to an unattacked square

steps.title: Exercise: Back-Rank Mate
steps.text: Black's King is trapped behind its own pawns on the back rank. Use your Rook on d1 to deliver checkmate!
steps.hint: Move your Rook all the way to d8 on Black's back rank.
steps.correctFeedback: Checkmate! The Black King has nowhere to run.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Play Rd8 to attack the King on the back rank.

steps.title: Stalemate vs Checkmate
steps.text: If a player has no legal moves and their King is NOT in check, what is the result of the game?

quizOptions.text: The player with more pieces wins.
quizOptions.explanation: Material count does not determine the game result in stalemate.

quizOptions.text: It is a Draw by Stalemate.
quizOptions.explanation: Correct! When a player cannot make any legal move and their King is safe from check, it is Stalemate, resulting in a draw (half point each).

quizOptions.text: The player whose turn it is loses on time.
quizOptions.explanation: No, this is a stalemate rule.

title: Basic Tactics: The Royal Fork
description: Discover how a single piece can attack multiple enemy targets at once.
objectives: Identify forking squares
Execute double attacks with Knights
Win material decisively

steps.title: What is a Fork?
steps.text: A 'fork' occurs when a single piece attacks two or more opponent pieces at the same time. Knights are notoriously dangerous forkers because they can leap over obstacles!

steps.title: Exercise: Fork King and Rook
steps.text: Black has an uncastled King on e8 and a Rook on a8. Jump your Knight from b5 to c7 to deliver check and win the Rook!
steps.hint: Jump your Knight into c7. It will attack both the King on e8 and the Rook on a8 simultaneously.
steps.correctFeedback: Brilliant! The King must move out of check, and on your next move you will capture the Rook.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Target square c7 is 2 squares up and 1 square right from b5.
